title: Quasi-coherent algebras on affine opens U ⊆ U': base change and the open immersion Spec A(U) → Spec A(U')
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal A$ a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For an affine open $U\subseteq S$ identify $U=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_S(U)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)\to U$ be induced by the structure map $\mathcal O_S(U)\to\mathcal A(U)$. Let $U\subseteq U'\subseteq S$ be affine opens, $R=\mathcal O_S(U)$, $R'=\mathcal O_S(U')$, $A=\mathcal A(U)$, $A'=\mathcal A(U')$. Then (i) the ring map $A'\otimes_{R'}R\to A$, $a'\otimes r\mapsto r\cdot a'|_U$, is an isomorphism; (ii) consequently the commutative square formed by $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ (induced by the restriction $A'\to A$), the structure morphisms, and the inclusion $U\hookrightarrow U'$ is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]; in particular $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ is an open immersion identifying $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, over $U$, with the preimage of $U$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(A')$; (iii) for affine opens $U\subseteq U'\subseteq U''$ the composition $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U')\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U'')$ is the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U'')$ of (ii), and for $U=U'$ the morphism is the identity.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN (label lemma-spec-inclusion, line 330 ff.; proof via Schemes, Lemma 01I9 lemma-widetilde-pullback, Lemma 01IA lemma-quasi-coherent-affine and Lemma 01JQ/lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes) and Lemma 01LO (label lemma-transitive-spec)

proof.text: *Sections over nested affine opens.* Forgetting the algebra multiplication, apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] to the quasi-coherent underlying module of $\mathcal A$. The resulting isomorphism $A'\otimes_{R'}R\cong A$ is compatible with multiplication and units because restriction and the tensor map are induced by the sheaf's $\mathcal O_S$-algebra structure; hence it is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN, first assertion; Schemes Lemmas 01I9 and 01IA

proof.text: *The cartesian square and the open immersion.* The fibre product of $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ with $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\to U'=\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ is, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}(A'\otimes_{R'}R)$. Step 1 identifies this ring with $A$, so the canonical square with $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ is cartesian. Since $U\hookrightarrow U'$ is an open immersion, its base change is an open immersion; thus $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with the preimage of $U$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01LN, second assertion; Schemes Lemmas 01JQ and 01JR

proof.text: *Transitivity.* For affine opens $U\subseteq U'\subseteq U''$, the restriction maps of the sheaf algebra compose, so the corresponding maps of spectra compose contravariantly. The identity restriction for $U=U'$ gives the identity morphism. Therefore the composite through $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U')$ equals the direct morphism from $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U'')$.
